title: Agreement with the bounded derived global sections
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme, $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, and $K\in D^+(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $C$ be a complex representing $K$ and let $a:C\to I$ and $b:C\to J=\operatorname{Kinj}(C)$ be K-injective resolutions [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]. Put $\Gamma(T,M)=M(T)$, with its $\Lambda$-module structure and applied termwise to complexes [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then the unbounded derived global sections $\RGamma(T_{\Et},K)=\Gamma(T,I)$ of [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded] is canonically isomorphic in $D(\Lambda)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to $\Gamma(T,J)$. Here $\Gamma(T,J)$ is the bounded-below K-injective construction of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], carried out in $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$; for $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$ it is exactly that definition. The comparison is the image under termwise global sections and localization of the unique homotopy class $u:I\to J$ with $u\circ a$ homotopic to $b$, and is natural in $K$.

proof.text: The Lean statement already supplies the complex C and both resolutions a:C→I and b:C→J. Unpack [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]: a and b are quasi-isomorphisms and I and J are K-injective. Their images under localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] are invertible. No additional resolution is chosen.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective, clauses (1) and (3); augmentation-compatible comparison and functoriality

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], lift (Qa)⁻¹ followed by Qb to a map u:I→J. Reflect equality under localization to obtain a≫u homotopic to b. A second compatible comparison has the same localization after cancelling Qa, so it is homotopic to u. Lift the inverse of Qu to v:J→I; reflect the two inverse equations to obtain u≫v homotopic to 1 and v≫u homotopic to 1. The private helpers exist_Q_map_of_kInjective and homotopy_of_Q_map_eq implement the quotient-comparison isomorphism and the surjectivity/injectivity of Qh_map_bijective.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective, clauses (1) and (3); augmentation-compatible comparison and functoriality

proof.text: Termwise global sections is additive, hence maps each inverse homotopy to a homotopy. Localization identifies homotopic maps, so QΓv is an explicit inverse to QΓu. Compute the unbounded functor [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded] on I using Functor.rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso, preceded by the image of eC⁻¹ followed by Qa. This yields eI:RΓ(K)≅QΓI. Define eJ=eI followed by the isomorphism with hom QΓu; its compatibility equation is definitional. Since the bounded-below recipe [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] uses the same module-sheaf sections, this gives the required agreement.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective, clauses (1) and (3); augmentation-compatible comparison and functoriality

proof.text: For f:QC→QC′, use [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] with targets I′ and J′ to lift (Qa)⁻¹≫f≫Qa′ and (Qb)⁻¹≫f≫Qb′ to p and q. Their augmentation equations follow by cancellation. For arbitrary p and q satisfying these equations, precompose Q(u≫q) and Q(p≫u′) with Qa. Both become f≫Qb′ by the two augmentation equations and the comparison equations for u and u′. Cancel Qa and reflect equality to a homotopy using the K-injectivity of J′. Termwise sections and localization send this homotopy to the asserted naturality square.
